parameters.query:
with due as (
  select l.id,
         exists (select 1
                   from sequence_steps s
                  where s.category = l.category and s.step = l.follow_up_step + 1) as has_template
    from leads l
   where l.status in ('new', 'contacted', 'nurturing')
     and l.next_follow_up_at <= now()
   order by l.next_follow_up_at
   limit 10
     for update of l skip locked
), closed as (
  -- the next step was removed from sequence_steps: end the sequence instead of waiting forever
  update leads l
     set next_follow_up_at = null,
         status = 'no_response',
         updated_at = now()
    from due
   where l.id = due.id and not due.has_template
  returning l.id
), claimed as (
  -- a 30 minute lease: if this run dies before recording the result,
  -- the lead becomes due again instead of being lost
  update leads l
     set next_follow_up_at = now() + interval '30 minutes',
         updated_at = now()
    from due
   where l.id = due.id and due.has_template
  returning l.id, l.email, l.full_name, l.company, l.category, l.follow_up_step + 1 as step,
            l.owner_email, l.response_token, l.opening
)
select c.*, s.subject, s.body,
       exists (select 1
                 from sequence_steps n
                where n.category = c.category and n.step = c.step + 1) as has_next_step
  from claimed c
  join sequence_steps s on s.category = c.category and s.step = c.step
 order by c.id

with updated as (
  update leads l
     set follow_up_step = $5::int,
         last_contacted_at = now(),
         next_follow_up_at = case when $3::boolean then
                               (select now() + s.delay_days::float8 * $2::interval
                                  from sequence_steps s
                                 where s.category = l.category and s.step = $5::int + 1)
                             end,
         status = case when not $3::boolean then 'no_response'
                       when l.status = 'new' then case when l.category = 'cold' then 'nurturing' else 'contacted' end
                       else l.status end,
         updated_at = now()
   where l.id = $1::bigint
     and l.status in ('new', 'contacted', 'nurturing')
  returning l.id, l.status, l.follow_up_step, l.next_follow_up_at
)
insert into lead_activities (lead_id, type, detail)
select id,
       case when follow_up_step = 0 then 'email_sent' else 'follow_up_sent' end,
       jsonb_build_object('step', follow_up_step, 'subject', $4::text,
                          'sequence_finished', status = 'no_response',
                          'next_follow_up_at', next_follow_up_at)
  from updated
returning lead_id

parameters.query:
with attempts as (
  select count(*) as failed_before
    from lead_activities
   where lead_id = $1::bigint
     and type = 'email_failed'
     and detail->>'step' = $2::text
), updated as (
  -- retry every 10 minutes, give up after the fifth failure of the same email
  update leads l
     set next_follow_up_at = case when (select failed_before from attempts) >= 4 then null
                                  else now() + interval '10 minutes' end,
         status = case when (select failed_before from attempts) >= 4 then 'undeliverable'
                       else l.status end,
         updated_at = now()
   where l.id = $1::bigint
     and l.status in ('new', 'contacted', 'nurturing')
  returning l.id, l.status
)
insert into lead_activities (lead_id, type, detail)
select id, 'email_failed',
       jsonb_build_object('step', $2::int, 'error', $3::text, 'gave_up', status = 'undeliverable')
  from updated
returning lead_id

parameters.content:
## Follow-ups
Runs every minute and picks up leads whose next email is due.

Up to 10 rows are claimed with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and leased for 30 minutes, so overlapping runs never email the same lead twice and a crash never loses a lead. A failed send is retried every 10 minutes; after five failures the lead is marked undeliverable.

Steps and copy come from the sequence_steps table. With DEMO_FAST_FOLLOW_UPS=true one "day" is one minute.
